reasoning_trace.value: The paper includes several figures, including Fig. 1, which illustrates the proposed system architecture for 6G ISAC services, and Fig. 2, which shows the sensing stream scheduling through optical transport switching. Fig. 3 compares the total volume of transmitted sensing traffic with and without optical network switching.

reasoning_trace.description: Explain the System Mechanism and ISAC Coupling Mode found.
reasoning_trace.value: The proposed system architecture adopts an optoelectronic transport network to interconnect the Radio Access Network (RAN) with the core functions located at edge and central cloud compute resources. The system uses a Doppler OFDM radar to sense the surrounding environment and detect moving targets. The OFDM waveform is organized into frames, and the echoes (reflections) and scattering of wireless signals provide information related to the characteristics of the environment and/or objects therein.

reasoning_trace.description: Validate the physical consistency of reported metrics (Rate/Resolution).
reasoning_trace.value: The paper reports on the volume of sensing traffic vs resolution velocity and the optical transport network capacity allocated for sensing with and without optical network switching. The results indicate that significant benefits in terms of network capacity reduction can be achieved across a variety of mobile target detection scenarios.

reasoning_trace.description: Identify the solved problems and remaining open challenges.
reasoning_trace.value: The paper proposes the adoption of optical switching technologies as an enabler in aggregating sensing streams in 6G networks supporting ISAC services. The results indicate that significant benefits in terms of network capacity reduction can be achieved. However, the paper also highlights the need for further research in optimizing the optical transport network resources for ISAC services.
